_comment: Example Sentry configuration file. Export a real one from a working instance (Settings > Download configuration, or GET /api/config) rather than hand-writing this — the shape is validated on import and an exported file is always correct. An export NEVER contains a password: not the hotspot's, and not the controller's. Two import-only keys may be hand-added to provision a fresh Pi in one step: "console_password" at the top level (sets the Sentry controller password, and only when the destination has none — a file cannot replace an existing one), and "passphrase" inside the hotspot section. Both are read on import and can never reappear in a file Sentry exports. Treat any file you add either to as a secret. Still absent entirely: the .env-only deploy gate SENTRY_HOTSPOT_CONTROL_ENABLED. See docs/adr/0007 and docs/adr/0010 for why. The "location" section is this Sentry's own fixed position, which Sentinel reads to plot it on a map; an export writes "" for both coordinates when none is set, and importing an empty section never clears a position the destination already has. It describes where the box physically sits rather than how it is configured, so set apply_location false when provisioning a *second* Pi from the first's file.
